answer: The ledger admits a new agent key only with a delay proof seeded by the previous registration's hash, so no proof can start before the last one lands, whether the agent hauls basalt freight or prices crops. In a 24-hour window, the k-th key needs 2^(k-1) minutes of serial squaring. Ten saffron-trading keys take 1,023 minutes, and the tenth alone takes 512. GPUs can't split a serial chain, so flooding orchard-yield markets stays out of reach.
